_comment: Connector-specific edits a cli-printing-press reprint must NOT clobber. check_handfixes.py asserts every marker below is still present and fails CI if a reprint dropped one. governance.md is preserved by onboard.py --resume but a FULL reprint re-runs gen_governance.py and would re-introduce the mis-tiering.

handfixes.summary: Hand-added an 'Endpoint / patch execution' tier; gen_governance is method-blind and missed all 31 POSTs (run-automation, approve-updates, remote-sessions, scripts)
handfixes.why: Action1 is a patch/RMM connector whose members RUN CODE/PATCHES on live managed endpoints. gen_governance.py keyword-matches and ignores pp:method, so it caught only -patch/-delete suffixes and missed every POST: `automations policies-instances-org-id-post` (run an automation), the stop-automation, `updates approvals updates-org-id` (approve updates for deployment), `endpoints ...-remote-sessions-post/-patch`, `installed-software requery ...post`, `scripts org-id-post`/`org-id-id-patch`. governance.md was rewritten method-aware from the authoritative agent-context pp:method. A full reprint re-runs the keyword classifier and drops these execution writes to Read. See project_action1_onboard_traps.

handfixes.summary: `oauth2` (mints a bearer token) + user/role management are in the Credential tier, not Read
handfixes.why: gen_governance put `(none detected)` for Credential and missed the `oauth2` token mint plus users/roles management entirely (method-blind, all POSTs). These touch identity/credentials and must be human-in-the-loop. A full reprint re-runs the classifier and leaves Credential empty. See project_action1_onboard_traps.

handfixes.summary: doctor probes a real GET endpoint with the real credential and refuses to dial a placeholder base_url, instead of calling any HTTP response 'reachable' and never checking the credential
handfixes.why: `doctor` is the command every SKILL, guide and docs page tells an operator to run to confirm the connector works, and it could not tell a working install from a broken one. It called any HTTP response to `GET /` "reachable" and rendered it green, so a base_url aimed at the vendor's web UI (where every API path 404s) and a token rejected with 401 on every call both produced an all-green report. On this connector family it also never probed the credential at all: it printed "present, not verified" and left the operator to guess. The mirror defect: a connector whose shipped base_url default is a placeholder dialled the placeholder host, and the DNS failure rendered as "FAIL API: unreachable" - telling a correctly-credentialled operator they were broken without naming the one variable that would fix it. Several placeholder hosts resolve through live wildcard DNS and answer real HTTP, so dialling one produced a confident green verdict against a stranger's server. Measured and gated by tools/maintainer/check_doctor_truth.py. See issue #282.

handfixes.summary: every operator credential this connector reads is declared on all three install channels: manifest.json (.mcpb), server.json (MCP Registry) and mcp-install.md (manual install)
handfixes.why: Issue #282 ('three live-verified connectors prompt for the wrong credentials'). A connector is installed through THREE independent channels that each carry their own copy of the credential list: manifest.json server.mcp_config.env (what the .mcpb bundle hands Claude Desktop, which has no shell profile, no config.toml and no export - so an undeclared variable is a variable nobody is ever asked for), server.json environmentVariables (the MCP Registry publish channel), and mcp-install.md's copy-paste JSON blocks plus its remote launch line (the manual path, which never touches the bundle at all). The fleet-wide audit found 60 of 65 connectors under-declaring 122 operator-facing variables in the manifest, 61 of 65 mcp-install.md pages omitting 125, and hudu's server.json missing the base URL its manifest marks required. For action1 the manifest gained: ACTION1_BASE_URL, ACTION1_OAUTH2, ACTION1_ORG_ID. Phantom prompt(s) the binary never reads were removed: ACTION1_REGION. server.json gained: ACTION1_BASE_URL, ACTION1_OAUTH2, ACTION1_ORG_ID. mcp-install.md's env blocks gained: ACTION1_BASE_URL, ACTION1_OAUTH2, ACTION1_ORG_ID. manifest.json, server.json and mcp-install.md are ALL regenerated by /msp-skills-publish on an UPDATE or re-onboard, so without this ledger a regeneration silently drops every declaration and CI stays green (check_env_schema.py is wired --warn). The asserts below name the specific credentials, not a count, so dropping one and adding another cannot cancel out.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should emit server.mcp_config.env, the matching user_config prompts, server.json environmentVariables and mcp-install.md's env blocks from ONE declaration of the connector's operator-facing environment, so the three channels cannot be generated out of step. Until then check_env_schema.py compares all three and this ledger pins them.

handfixes.summary: The MCP shell-out layer refuses filesystem-destination flags (--db, --input, --output, --out, --home, --audit-dir, --receipt-file and friends) and any argument name carrying '=', so a tool call cannot point the local SQLite store, or any other file this account can reach, at a path of its choosing
handfixes.why: The MCP server runs the companion CLI as the server account and forwarded every command-local flag straight through as a CLI argument. `sync` and the other local-store commands expose --db, and the store's migration runs `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS resources_fts` plus a resources-table rebuild against whatever file it is handed, so one tool call shaped {"db": "/path/to/someone-elses.sqlite"} rewrote an unrelated database - no credentials required, because sync opens the store before it ever reaches the API. Proven end to end: against the pre-fix binary a single MCP tools/call on `sync` changed the victim file's sha and left resources_fts with 0 rows; against the patched binary the same call returns the same sync summary and the victim file is byte-identical. The gate has three parts, all in cli/internal/mcp/cobratree/shellout.go: blockedDestinationFlags (the runtime name floor, unioned into cliArgsFromMCP alongside the pre-existing blockedRootFlags behaviour, which is unchanged); an argument-name '=' guard, because "db=/tmp/evil" was emitted as --db=/tmp/evil and a name-only denylist never saw it; and isFilesystemPathFlag, which classifies a flag by its USAGE TEXT rather than its NAME. The usage-text test is load bearing and must not be turned into a name rule: the generated command surface carries API body fields called --path, --seed-path, --source-paths, --exclude-paths, --filename and --working-dir whose values go to the vendor API and never touch this account's disk, so a name rule would break real API surfaces while still missing the next generated flag that does take a local path. UnblockedFilesystemPathFlags applies that rule to the live Cobra tree over exactly the command set RegisterAll turns into shell-out tools (endpoint and framework commands are out of scope, which is what keeps the rule off generated vendor body fields), and TestNoShellOutToolCanDirectAFilesystemPath fails the build when a regeneration grows a local-path flag the floor does not name. vendorAPIPathFlags is the documented exception list for flags whose usage trips the rule but which name a location in the vendor's world. Both directions are pinned by the tests: the --db argument must be dropped AND an ordinary flag must still be forwarded, because a gate that swallows the real MCP surface is as harmful as one that misses the defect.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: the gate belongs in the generator. Two known residuals a reprint should close rather than re-inherit. (1) On the pre-4.30 cobratree the blocked flags are dropped at forward time but still appear in the tool's input schema, because toolOptionsForFlags in typemap.go advertises every flag; the caller gets silence instead of an error. The 4.30 shape (blockedStructuredArgsForCommand + allowedStructuredArgsForCommand) removes them from the schema and errors on them, which is the better behaviour. (2) isFilesystemPathFlag is only consulted by the package test here, not at request time, because the pre-4.30 shellOutToCLI receives no *cobra.Command; wiring it into the per-command blocked set (as skills/servosity does) makes a newly generated path flag refused at runtime rather than at CI time.

handfixes.summary: Load marks ClientID/ClientSecret as env overrides, configForSave restores the file value, and SaveTokens keeps both markers, so env-supplied OAuth credentials are never written to config.toml (issue #266)
handfixes.why: This connector shipped the defect issue #266 fixed elsewhere in the fleet, and it shipped a WORSE version of it: Load() did not mark ClientID/ClientSecret as env overrides at all AND configForSave() restored only Action1Oauth2, so `out := *c` copied the live env-supplied client_secret straight into the saved struct. internal/client/oauth_cc.go calls SaveTokens on every automatic client-credentials mint, which is an ordinary authenticated command and not an explicit login step, so ACTION1_CLIENT_ID and ACTION1_CLIENT_SECRET landed in ~/.config/action1-cli/config.toml in cleartext - defeating the Keychain / Credential-Manager setups that inject them as environment variables at process launch. The fix is the fleet's: mark both in Load, restore both in configForSave, and stop SaveTokens clearing the two markers. Provenance must be DECLARED, not inferred: comparing the incoming value against the loaded one cannot tell an explicit flag from the environment value it happens to duplicate, so MarkCredentialsExplicit is the only thing that clears a marker. GENERATOR-class defect (the press emits both the missing marks and the unconditional deletes); a reprint reintroduces the leak and these markers guard the connector. Bug-fix-only: no new flag, command, or output.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press#4283 plus the missing half here: Load() must markEnvOverride EVERY env-sourced credential field it assigns, and configForSave() must restore every one it marked. action1 was emitted with the marker on the connector-specific oauth2 field only, so the generic ClientID/ClientSecret pair - the fields the OAuth client-credentials mint actually writes - were unprotected in both directions at once.

asserts.contains: markers now survive a save; only MarkCredentialsExplicit clears them.

handfixes.summary: ACTION1_NO_CONFIG_WRITE makes every credential write a no-op (token cache included) while leaving the `auth logout` erase working, and the MCP server honours it too (issue #270)
handfixes.why: Issue #270, raised by @Xenith-B off the back of #266. #266 stopped env-supplied client credentials reaching disk; the MINTED access token still landed in ~/.config/<tool>-cli/config.toml in cleartext and there was no supported way to turn that off. Their workaround was `--config NUL`, which is OS-specific, undocumented, makes doctor report a false 'not configured', and - the part that matters most - does not cover the MCP servers at all, because internal/mcp resolved its own hardcoded config path and ignored --config. Three deliberate boundaries make this switch honest rather than merely quiet. (1) ClearTokens keeps calling save() directly: it is the ERASE path, and routing it through the guard would make `auth logout` silently inert, which is a worse defect than the one being fixed. (2) `auth set-token`, the only command on this connector that writes a credential on purpose (its `auth --help` lists logout, set-token, setup, status), REFUSES and names the variable rather than reporting a save that did not happen - a false success is the same defect class as a doctor that says credentials are fine without checking. (3) newMCPClient now resolves through config.Load(""), the resolver the CLI uses, so the MCP server honours both ACTION1_CONFIG and this switch; that is the half the issue says is uncovered today. The variable is declared on all three install channels because for a Claude Desktop install the manifest prompt is the ONLY channel that can set an environment variable. Class C, new documented surface. GENERATOR-class: a reprint drops the switch entirely and silently restores the plaintext token cache.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should emit <PREFIX>_NO_CONFIG_WRITE (or an equivalent) as part of the standard config surface, with the same three boundaries: the erase path exempt, explicit save commands failing loudly rather than no-oping, and the MCP server resolving its config through config.Load("") instead of a hardcoded home-relative path. The hardcoded path in internal/mcp/tools.go is a generator defect in its own right - it makes --config and <PREFIX>_CONFIG inert for every MCP install on every connector.

asserts.contains: | `auth set-token` | Refuses, naming the variable, instead of reporting a save that did not happen. |
